conditions: The event is on Jordan Lee's calendar (the calendar being acted on).
The event's subject matter is a 'product demo dry run' — a rehearsal for a product demo.
The event has a Google Meet link.
The event has the Bridgewater room booked.
Exactly one event matches all conditions (the request treats it as unique).
The action requested is cancellation of that event.

readings: The event's own status is Confirmed (as opposed to Tentative or Cancelled)
Jordan Lee's personal RSVP response to the event is 'Yes/Accepted' (as opposed to Tentative/Declined)
The event has Google Meet conferencing actually attached via calendar's video-call integration (conferenceData)
The event's description or location merely contains a meet.google.com URL as text, without a real attached conference
A calendar room resource named 'Bridgewater' is added to the event as a booked resource
The location field just names 'Bridgewater' as text, without an actual room resource booking
A specific event titled exactly something like 'Product Demo Dry Run'
Any rehearsal-type event for a product demo, regardless of exact title wording (e.g., 'Demo Rehearsal', 'Dry Run - Product Demo')

records.note: Meets all conditions: title matches, status confirmed, has hangout_link, and Bridgewater room attendee has resource:true (actually booked).

Correct title, real Meet link, real Bridgewater room booking (resource:true), but status is tentative, not confirmed. No RSVP data exists for Jordan Lee, so event status is the only signal, and it fails c2.

turn2.differences: The author's four conditions match the substantive selectors from step 1 (title, confirmed status, Meet link, Bridgewater room booking). Omitted step-1 items ('on Jordan Lee's calendar', 'unique match') are trivial here since every record is on Jordan's calendar and exactly one satisfies all four conditions, so the omission doesn't change the outcome. The cancellation action is the requested operation, not a selection condition, so correctly left out.

ambiguity_effects.explain: Could mean event status or personal RSVP, but Jordan Lee has no attendee/RSVP record on any event, so only the event-status field is available. The ambiguity doesn't produce a different selection here.
Could mean an attached Meet conference vs. a meet.google.com URL in text. A careful reader defaults to the attached-conference reading, which is what makes ev_demo_nolink fail while the others pass.
Could mean an actual resource booking vs. a guest with that name. A careful reader requires the resource flag, which separates ev_demo_guestroom (fails) from ev_demo_confirmed (passes).
Could mean exact title vs. any rehearsal-type event, but every demo-related record shares the identical summary, so this ambiguity has no effect on the outcome here.

turn2.naturalness_note: Plausible as something a real user would say when disambiguating among several similar 'dry run' events on their calendar. Stacking three qualifying clauses is somewhat more enumerated than typical casual speech, a mild tell of a constructed scenario, but not implausible.
